 Judgment

These appeals are filed by both the claimant and the insurance company aggrieved by the award passed in NC: 2023:KHC:33834 M.V.C.No.178/2014 dated 22.11.2016 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT at Kundapura whereby the Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.1,67,630/-.
Both the insurance company as well as the claimant have preferred these appeals.

The claimant's appeal is numbered as M.F.A.No.667/2017 and the insurance company's appeal is numbered as M.F.A.No.350/2017.
2.
The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.15,00,000/- and the Tribunal had awarded an amount of Rs.1,67,630/-.

It is the case of the claimant that on 28.01.2014 at about 7:10 p.m., the claimant was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motor cycle driven by his friend, from Tallur side towards Kundapura side in a slow manner and when the said motor cycle reached near Adarsha Hospital, Kundapura, Kasaba Village, on NH-66, Kundapura, at that time, a Mini Insulator Van driven by its driver in a high speed and rash and negligent manner came from Kundapura side towards Tallur side and dashed to the claimant's motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the claimant sustained grievous injuries.

According to the claimant, he was doing electrical work and earning an amount of Rs.18,000/- per month and he had spent an amount NC: 2023:KHC:33834 of Rs.2,00,000/- for treatment, nourishing food, medicine, attendant charges and another amount of Rs.50,000/- is required towards future treatment.
3.

When it comes to the liability, it is the case of the insurance company that the vehicle is registered as a medium goods vehicle and the driver of the vehicle was possessing a light motor vehicle transport.
It is submitted that as there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

Considering the judgment in the case of Smt.Sandhya Sudhakaran And Others Vs. Considering the arguments of the learned counsel for the respondent that the vehicle's weight is 1960 Kgs, the Court below has held that while considering the category of the vehicle, laden weight is not the criteria but unladden weight is the criteria.
When the unladen weight does not exceed 4080 Kgs, the said contention cannot be considered.
In this case, the vehicle itself is registered as a medium goods vehicle and the driver of the vehicle was having only the license to drive light motor vehicle.
On the face of it, it appears that there is violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.
In view of the same, this Court is of the view that the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
5. Considering Exs.R.1, R.2 and R.3, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

Coming to the injuries sustained by the claimant, as per Ex.P.4, he has sustained five injuries, C.T. Scan shows fracture of anterior and posterior acromia walls of left nasal of sinus, fracture of zygomatic arch, lateral wall with orbit wall.
Considering these injuries, the Court below had granted an amount of Rs.40,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the said amount was not a reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
The fracture of anterior and posterior acromia walls of left nasal of sinus and the fracture of NC: 2023:KHC:33834 zygomatic arch takes a lot of time to heal and it is a very painful thing.
Considering the same, this Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.70,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
Then coming to food, nourishment and attendant charges, transportation, as this requires extra nourishment and also attendant, he is entitled for an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
Towards medical bills, the Court below granted an amount of Rs.24,125/- which is a reasonable amount.

Towards loss of income also,
considering an amount of Rs.7,500/- for three months, the Court below had granted an amount of Rs.22,500/- which is also reasonable.
Then towards loss of amenities, the Court below granted an amount of Rs.15,000/- considering the kind of injuries the claimant has sustained.
This Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.30,000/- under the said head.
In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V.MEKALA vs. M. MALATHI AND ANOTHER2, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards legal expenses.
